text: QUANTUM ATOMS · FIXED INPUTS · VERIFIED CODE Hydrogenic atoms and helium: runnable validation examples From analytic references to self-consistency: run hydrogenic radial equations and closed-shell HF / exchange-only LDA for helium, with measured errors and explicit limits. Two problem families; 23 packaged checks passed. The ZIP was independently extracted and its fixed-input calculations and figures reproduced. Shared execution and validation guide for Barnes–Hut, hydrogenic atoms and helium Wide tables and equations scroll horizontally. Atomic units: hartree for energy and bohr for distance. Nonrelativistic, infinite-mass point nuclei, isolated boundaries and second-order uniform radial differences. Helium is restricted to spherical 1s² with two electrons and no correlation energy. Only for this two-electron, single-spatial-orbital HF problem, exchange cancels half the Hartree term: v_eff=−2/r+v_H/2 and E_x=−E_H/2. General HF exchange is not a local potential. LDA here is spin-unpolarized Dirac exchange only, without VWN or other correlation. p(r)=4πr²n(r), distinct from the three-dimensional density n. Each profile integrates to two electrons. Convergence requires all three: input-output density L1 residual <10⁻⁹, energy change <10⁻¹⁰ hartree, and output-density orbital residual <10⁻⁷ hartree. An alternative initial density and mixing 0.7 are checked. Normalization imposes electron number, which is also tested. Not a general molecular, periodic or many-electron solver. Checks cover analytic states, charge scaling, orthogonality, a dense eigensolver, analytic exponential-density Hartree fields, exchange differentiation, grid/domain convergence, starts, failure and independent implementations. H₂, general many-electron HF, LDA correlation/GGA/hybrids, periodic k sampling and numerical band-irrep validation remain next.
